study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Xiao et al., Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Deviations From Normative Functioning Underlying Emotional Episodic Memory Revealed Cross-Scale Neurodiverse Alterations Linked to Affective Symptoms in Distinct Psychiatric Disorders

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Use normative modeling of task-fMRI activation during an emotional episodic memory task to quantify individualized deviations in MDD, BD, and SZ; embed deviations in large-scale emotional networks and relate them to affective symptoms and cell-type signatures via imaging transcriptomics.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Healthy dataset (Peking University Center for MRI Research, HCtrain)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The normative reference was trained on a large healthy control cohort (HCtrain) recruited at Peking University Center for MRI Research; no other named public dataset was used.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: "The healthy dataset included 409 healthy controls (HCtrain) were recruited from the Center for MRI Research, Peking University."

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: The reference cohort (HCtrain) was acquired at one site and the clinical/test data at another. The paper does not mention any explicit method for site-effect correction (e.g., ComBat). It validates model generalizability across sites but does not appear to harmonize the data itself.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Imaging data were acquired from participants on a 3T GE Discovery MR750 scanner in the Center for MRI Research, Peking University (healthy dataset) and the Center for Neuroimaging, Peking University Sixth Hospital (clinical dataset).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Distinct, diagnosis-specific deviation patterns in emotional networks predict affective symptoms; cell-type enrichment implicates microglia (MDD), astrocytes (BD), and excitatory neurons (SZ).
